newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse heads higher again, future unclear.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse heads higher again, future unclear.

text.p: The Brussels bourse headed higher on Wednesday after an early spate of selling gave way to a flurry of buying to end the three-day decline that was triggered by strong U.S. data last Friday.
But traders said it was impossible to tell if the recovery, in tandem with other European bourses, was the real thing or simply a blip.
"It really all depends on the dollar and the mark," one trader said. "The threat of a German interest rate rise is still a major factor hanging over the market."

The Buba may be forced to act if the dollar's rise looks like stoking inflation, they said. Traders said it was too early to tell if Wednesday's rise in Belgian petrol prices to record levels -- due in part to the rampant dollar -- was the first sign of imported inflation or simply an anomaly.
Wednesday's twin stars were steelmakers Arbed and Cockerill Sambre, up 7.1 percent and 3.8 percent respectively.

Traders said the rise was in part due to an improving outlook for the sector and partly to favourable reactions to Arbed's recent Spanish acquisition. They noted that Arbed had risen 20 percent since the news.

Chemicals and drugs firm UCB, which plunged after news last week of half year results up 33 percent and in line with expectations, added to a recovery that started Tuesday, rising 1.5 percent to 129,600 francs.
Retailers Colruyt and Quick, and insurer Royale Belge were also up around 1.5 percent.
Oil major PetroFina, which rallied last week after strong first half results but then suffered from profit-taking earlier this week, recovered to add 1.2 percent at 14,700 francs.
At 0940 GMT the Bel-20 index of blue chip shares was 7.82 points or 0.32 percent up 2,463.54, having swung in a 2,477.50/2,443.89 range.
There were 12 gainers, two unchanged and six losers.
Traders said that by comparison with the first two days of the week the market was relatively busy.
